title: Follow-the-sun oncall rollout brief (scratch)
content:
Purpose: Draft internal announcement + all-hands talking points + FAQ for rolling our new follow-the-sun oncall model for infra/SRE. This is a personal scratchpad — not final. Primary goal is to reduce off-hours fatigue for US night engineers and improve international coverage reliability.

Audience: SRE, infra, serving-runtime eng leads, people ops (scheduling), support escalation leads, engineering managers.

High-level rollout timeline (proposal):
- Phase 0 (pilot): 6 weeks, starting 2026-01-05. Pilot with 2 cross-region pods (serving-runtime + infra).
- Phase 1 (expand): 8 weeks after pilot review — include console-and-tooling SRE.
- Phase 2 (company-wide default): target 2026-04.

What we intend to change (short):
- Move from majority-US oncall to geographically distributed 24x7 coverage by regionally-based volunteers + rotation.
- Shift primary pager ownership to the local region in nighttime hours (APAC/EU), with defined escalation to US L2 for complex incidents.
- Formalize handoff artifacts: short context (what to know), active incident list, outstanding postmortem owners.

Why now (talking points):
- Measured burnout signals: increased after-hours escalations in last 12 months, rising paging noise for the small US night team.
- We have improved automation, better playbooks, and regionally staffed capacity to make follow-the-sun viable.
- Expected benefits: faster local responses, lower average time-to-ack, better sleep for US nights.
- Risks: coordination slips, unfamiliarity with legacy runbooks; mitigations below.

Proposed communications cadence:
- Week -2: Informal heads-up to SRE and infra leads in Slack; collect volunteers for pilot.
- Week -1: Send pilot kickoff email to participating teams with schedule and expectations.
- Day 0 (pilot start): Short announcement in #sre, #eng-all and a calendar invite for sync.
- Weekly: pilot retro notes and metrics snapshot (MTTA/MTTR/pager volume).

Sample Slack announcement (short):
"Heads up — starting Jan 5 we're launching a 6-week pilot of a follow-the-sun oncall for infra + serving-runtime. Goal: reduce night burden on US engineers and improve regional response. If you want to be part of the pilot, ping @Rowan or sign up in the doc. We'll post playbooks and a short onboarding session. This is a pilot; feedback is critical."

Onboarding for pilots:
- 60-min async onboarding: playbook walkthrough + runbook quick-checklist.
- Pairing: first two shifts paired with existing US L2 to shadow (virtual handover).
- Access: ensure VPN/KMS/monitoring dashboards available for regional assignees.

Operational playbook changes (short bullets):
- New shift template: shift-start checklist, triage quickscript, escalation matrix (regional -> US L2 -> oncall PM).
- Handover artifact: single-line summary + top-3 followups + active incidents; stored in incident tracker.
- Pager filters: fine-tune thresholding for non-actionable noise (alert categorization update).

FAQ (working):
Q: Will this increase our oncall headcount?
A: Pilot uses volunteers from existing regional teams; long-term we may formalize modest FTE allocation for 24x7 coverage. Not an immediate hiring ask.

Q: What about knowledge gaps for regionally-based engineers?
A: We'll run playbook reviews, pair first two shifts with US L2, and maintain a short region-specific runbook. Plus office-hours with original oncall owners.

Q: How will we measure success?
A: Metrics: MTTA (target -20% during pilot nights), MTTR (target -5%), pager volume per-person (target -25% for US night assignees), qualitative feedback from retros.

Q: How do escalations work across timezones?
A: Default: regional assignee -> regional senior -> US L2 oncall if needed. Escalation timings mirrored in playbook with clear SLAs (e.g., 15 min ack target for Sev2).

Risks and mitigations (notes):
- Risk: misconfigured dashboards or perms block regional response. Mitigation: permissions audit before pilot; integrated checklist.
- Risk: inconsistent triage. Mitigation: standardized triage quickscript and 1:1 shadowing for two shifts.

Metrics dashboard (what I'll ask analytics for):
- Pager volume by hour and by assignee region (last 90 days).
- MTTA/MTTR split by timezone.
- Number of incidents requiring cross-region escalation.

Initial retro agenda (end of pilot):
- What worked / didn't (10m each).
- Data review (15m).
- Action items and ownership (15m).

Open questions (to decide before comms):
- Minimum team size per region to join pilot? (2 recommended)
- Formal compensation / recognition for night coverage (swaps, pager credit)? work with people ops
- Should we lock a fixed regional L2 or make it rotating?

Draft all-hands speaking bullets (30–60s):
- "We're piloting a follow-the-sun oncall to improve reliability and reduce night-time pressure on our US engineers. Pilot starts Jan 5 with two pods. We expect faster local responses and fewer high-noise pages for US nights. We'll share results and next steps after 6 weeks — feedback welcome."

Notes to self (scratch):
- Coordinate with People Ops for volunteer incentives before Week -2.
- Prepare a 20-min recorded onboarding walkthrough; post to SRE Playbooks.
- Confirm SSO/VPN perms for APAC contractors.

Next steps (me):
- Draft pilot signup doc and onboarding checklist (due 2025-11-15).
- Run permissions audit with infra team (due 2025-11-22).
- Schedule 1:1 with Rowan to align escalation matrix (this week).

Revision history: personal scratchpad, likely many iterations. Keep this file as a working version until we have pilot signups.
